subject: Re: Redline request — staged financial liability & termination conditioning
messages:
From: Derek Shaw <derek.shaw@healthsys.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@healthsys.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA liability — request for staged fee-at-risk and termination conditioning

Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed internally, HealthSys needs stronger commercial remedies than standard service credits for certain regulated lines of business. I'm attaching an updated SLA appendix (HealthSys_SLA_req_v3.pdf) that shows the remedies we're requesting:

- A staged fee-at-risk pool equal to 10% of monthly committed fees held in escrow and released monthly unless severity-1 or severity-2 misses occur (we propose a 2-quarter lookback).
- Early termination right (without penalty) if there are three S1 incidents impacting >10% of requests in a 90-day window.
- Liquidated damages alternative only where credits are insufficient to make HealthSys whole for downstream regulatory fines.

We understand Redwood's desire to limit exposure, but for regulated workflows we need an ability to remediate economically and terminate if reliability is repeatedly insufficient. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept staged escrow + a conditional termination right? If not, what alternatives do you propose that provide similar operational comfort?

Thanks,
Derek
Derek Shaw
VP, Platform Engineering — HealthSys

Attachment: HealthSys_SLA_req_v3.pdf (PDF, 230KB)
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Derek Shaw <derek.shaw@healthsys.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA liability — request for staged fee-at-risk and termination conditioning

Derek,

Appreciate the clear appendix. Short answer up front: we recognize the ask and can do a compromise that balances HealthSys's regulatory needs with Redwood's operational risk. High-level counterproposal below; legal (Karthik) is cc'd to capture the contract language.

- Fee-at-risk: Redwood can agree to a time-limited escrow of up to 7% of committed monthly fees, released monthly absent qualifying incidents. We need to limit the escrow percentage and define qualifying incidents precisely (S1/S2 definitions and measurable impact thresholds).
- Termination: Redwood is open to a conditional termination right after two qualifying S1 incidents within a 120-day rolling window that cause sustained degraded throughput or latency above the agreed thresholds AND where Redwood cannot restore service to agreed QoS within an agreed remediation window. We cannot accept an open-ended 3x trigger tied only to % of requests without an operational remediation step.
- Liquidated damages: we push back on open-ended LDs. If HealthSys insists, we can offer capped LDs tied to documented regulatory penalties (with a cap equal to 50% of 6 months' committed fees) and only after exhaustion of credits and escrow.

Next steps: if that high-level is acceptable, Karthik will draft contract language, and we will ask Ops to provide our incident measurement plan (SLOs, tooling, lookback windows). Would you be comfortable with a 7% escrow and the 2-incident + remediation-window termination approach?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick reply and the alternative. A few clarifying points from our side before you and Karthik draft contract language:

- The primary reason we asked for 10% is that some months our regulated workloads will generate material downstream liability if inference is materially wrong or unavailable; 7% increases our exposure. Could Redwood cap the escrow at 7% but provide a mechanism to increase to 10% in defined breach windows (for example, after the first qualifying S1 and until the issue is remediated)?
- On termination, our ask is that the remedy be available without a protracted try-fix loop if the vendor repeatedly misses the SLOs. We could agree to an operational remediation step, but we need measurable gates (MTTR commitments, RCA timelines) and a maximum overall cure period.
- For LDs, HealthSys can provide a formula tied to documented regulatory fines. We would prefer LDs to be payable only when fines are actually levied, not on a per-incident basis.

Please also confirm whether Redwood would accept a 90-day lookback for termination triggers (we had proposed 90 earlier; your note suggested 120).

Regards,
Derek
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Derek / HealthSys team,

Thanks for the thoughtful framing. I've worked with Finance and Legal on a redline that I think will get us to an executable position while protecting both parties. Key points of Redwood's proposed contract language:

1) Escrow / Fee-at-risk: 7% of committed monthly fees held in escrow. After a qualifying S1 incident, Redwood will allow an interim increase to 10% for up to 60 days while remediation and a joint-impact assessment are conducted; any extension beyond 60 days requires mutual written agreement. Escrow funds are released monthly absent qualifying incidents.

2) Termination trigger: HealthSys may terminate for convenience without penalty if there are two qualifying S1 incidents within a 90-day rolling window AND Redwood fails to meet the agreed remediation plan (including MTTR and RCA milestones) within 30 calendar days of the second incident. This provides a clear cure window and objective remediation gates.

3) Liquidated damages: LDs are only payable where HealthSys can demonstrate a regulatory fine directly attributable to service unavailability or wrongful outputs, subject to a cap equal to 50% of six months' committed fees. LDs are a remedy of last resort after escrow and credits are exhausted.

4) Measurement and tooling: We will include an incident measurement appendix that defines severity tiers, measurement of impacted request % (sampling and telemetry requirements), and required post-incident artifacts (RCA within 10 business days).

I've attached a draft redline and the proposed incident appendix (see related links). If HealthSys accepts the 60-day interim escrow increase and the 30-day cure window, I think we can move quickly to execution. Happy to hop on a call on Monday to walk through the language.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
